title: Finite direct diagrams in a Brown localization
statement:
Use quasicategories, nerves, coherent functor categories and equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], in sufficiently large universes. Let $\mathcal A$ be an ordinary category with initial object $0$ and classes $C,W$ of arrows containing isomorphisms and closed under composition. Suppose $W$ has two-out-of-three and is retract closed, every $0\to X$ belongs to $C$, every arrow factors as a member of $C$ followed by a member of $W$, pushouts of members of $C$ along arbitrary arrows exist and belong to $C$, and pushouts of members of $C\cap W$ belong to $C\cap W$. Let $q:N(\mathcal A)\to L$ be its homotopy coherent localization, universal on entire coherent functor categories for inverting $W$. Let $I$ be an ordinary category with finitely many objects and morphisms and a degree function to $\mathbf N$ such that every nonidentity arrow strictly raises degree. Let $W_I$ be the natural transformations of strict functors $I\to\mathcal A$ whose components belong to $W$. Evaluation and $q$ induce an equivalence
$$N(\operatorname{Fun}(I,\mathcal A))[W_I^{-1}]_\infty\simeq\operatorname{Fun}(N(I),L).$$
Moreover every coherent diagram $N(I)\to L$ is coherently naturally equivalent to $q\circ N(D)$ for some strict $D:I\to\mathcal A$. In particular every object of $L$ is equivalent to some $qX$. The empty category, the singleton and the span category $(0\leftarrow1\to2)$ are allowed. No arbitrary coproducts, functorial factorization, fibrations or model structure are assumed.

source.place: Dual of Theorem 7.6.17, printed pp. 394-395 (PDF pp. 409-410), and the localization construction of section 7.1 (essential surjectivity on objects); ordinary all-cofibrant case of Definition 7.4.12. No Stacks tag states this coherent rectification result. Read online on 2026-10-17; not archived in literature/.

proof.text: We first establish the inverse-diagram assertion for an ordinary all-fibrant Brown category with retract-closed weak equivalences $\mathcal C$, with $q:N\mathcal C\to L\mathcal C$: a terminal object $1$, classes $W,F$ containing isomorphisms and closed under composition, $W$ retract closed with two-out-of-three, every $X\to1$ in $F$, pullbacks of members of $F$ (resp. $F\cap W$) existing and lying in $F$ (resp. $F\cap W$), and $W$-then-$F$ factorizations; these are the hypotheses of [lem-coef-brown-reedy-fibrant-replacement] together with retract closure. Then $\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}$, with initial object $1$, cofibrations $F^{\mathrm{op}}$ and weak equivalences $W^{\mathrm{op}}$, satisfies the hypotheses of [lem-coef-brown-left-fractions], and $q^{\mathrm{op}}:N(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}})\to(L\mathcal C)^{\mathrm{op}}$ is a localization in its sense (test the universal property on opposite targets and reverse coherent functors and transformations). Reversing its conclusions gives the Brown fractions of $\mathcal C$ used below: every object of $L\mathcal C$ is equivalent to some $qX$; every $\alpha:qX\to qY$ satisfies $[\alpha]=[q(a)][q(s)]^{-1}$ in $hL\mathcal C$ with $s:Z\to X$ in $F\cap W$ and $a:Z\to Y$; and for $u:X\to Y$, $[q(u)]$ has a right inverse if and only if there is $v:Z\to X$ in $F$ with $uv\in W$, so such a fibration $v$ exists whenever $q(u)$ is invertible. They apply equally to $R_J$ and $R_K$, which step 4 shows are Brown categories of this kind. At the end take $\mathcal C=\mathcal A^{\mathrm{op}}$. For a finite inverse category $K$ write $R_K$ for the Reedy fibrant strict diagrams of [lem-coef-brown-reedy-fibrant-replacement]. Its localized inclusion identifies $L(R_K)$ with the localization of all strict $K$-diagrams. Evaluation therefore gives the canonical comparison $F_K:L(R_K)\to\operatorname{Fun}(N(K),L\mathcal C)$. Localization of $\mathcal C$ exists and has finite limits by [lem-coef-brown-fibrant-localization-pullbacks].

source.place: Theorem 7.6.17, first paragraph; Theorems 7.4.20 and 7.5.18; dual of Corollary 7.5.19 and formula (7.2.10.4)

proof.text: Put $\mathcal E_K=\operatorname{Fun}(N(K),L\mathcal C)$. Brown localization supplies finite coherent limits in $L\mathcal C$. First translate between the limiting cones of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] and the relative diagrams of [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone]. For a small simplicial set $M$ and a quasicategory $\mathcal Q$, [lem-coef-infinity-join-cone-calculus] makes every coherent cone $\Delta_Mx\to F$ equivalent to the cone of a join diagram $M^{\triangleleft}\to\mathcal Q$, and its mapping formula shows that a join diagram is a limit diagram relative to $\mathcal Q\to\Delta^0$ exactly when its cone is limiting: the base of the relative square is a point, and testing against the constant cone at $y$ recovers the map $\operatorname{Map}(y,x)\to\operatorname{Map}(\Delta_My,F)$ of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. By clause (4) of [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-equivalence] these are exactly the opposites of colimit diagrams relative to $\mathcal Q^{\mathrm{op}}\to\Delta^0$, and reversing simplices identifies $\mathcal E_K^{\mathrm{op}}$ with $\operatorname{Fun}(N(K)^{\mathrm{op}},(L\mathcal C)^{\mathrm{op}})$. Now use [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cocone-parameters] with the inner fibration $U:(L\mathcal C)^{\mathrm{op}}\to\Delta^0$ and $B=N(K)^{\mathrm{op}}$. For a finite shape, choose limiting evaluated cones in $L\mathcal C$ and prescribe their join representatives; the extension clause gives a cone in $\mathcal E_K$ with exactly these evaluations. The recognition clause makes every cone with limiting evaluations a $U_B$-colimit after reversal; since $\operatorname{Fun}(B,\Delta^0)=\Delta^0$, the translation shows it is limiting in $\mathcal E_K$. Thus $\mathcal E_K$ has finite coherent limits, detected at vertices, including terminal and pullback cones. This uses relative universality for postcomposition to the terminal category, not for restriction to vertices.

source.place: Opposite duals of Proposition 7.1.8.3 and Corollary 7.1.8.8; finite-vertex case of the original step 2.

proof.text: For $T_K:N(R_K)\to\mathcal E_K$, $X\mapsto qX$, the image of the terminal diagram is terminal: its evaluations are $q1$, terminal by the Brown localization lemma, so the vertex detection of step 2, from [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cocone-parameters], applies. For a pullback along a Reedy fibration, the Reedy lemma says the square is computed objectwise and every component of its fibration leg is a fibration in $\mathcal C$. The Brown localization lemma therefore makes each evaluated image square a coherent pullback; the same vertex detection of step 2 makes the image square a pullback in $\mathcal E_K$. Finally an objectwise weak equivalence is sent by $q$ to an equivalence at every vertex; the component criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] makes its $T_K$-image an equivalence.

source.place: Theorem 7.6.17, first paragraph; Propositions 7.5.5-7.5.6 and 7.5.28; parameter-cone construction as in section 6.4

proof.text: The Reedy lemma gives the all-fibrant Brown axioms for $R_K$. Its weak equivalences are retract closed: evaluate any retract of natural transformations at $k$ and use retract closure of $W$ in $\mathcal C$. The Brown localization lemma applied to $R_K$ gives finite limits in $L(R_K)$. Apply [lem-coef-brown-right-exact-extension] to $T_K^{\mathrm{op}}$, with all-cofibrant category $R_K^{\mathrm{op}}$, cofibrations opposite Reedy fibrations, and target $\mathcal E_K^{\mathrm{op}}$. Opposite arrows turn the verified terminal-object and fibration-pullback properties into its initial-object and cofibration-pushout hypotheses; the preceding step verifies that weak equivalences are inverted. Both source localization and target have finite colimits, since their opposites have finite limits. To identify the source localization, for every target $D$ reverse functors and transformations to identify $\operatorname{Fun}(L(R_K)^{\mathrm{op}},D)$ with $\operatorname{Fun}(L(R_K),D^{\mathrm{op}})^{\mathrm{op}}$, and apply the localization universal property. This gives precisely the weak-equivalence-inverting full functor category out of $N(R_K^{\mathrm{op}})$. Thus the extension is $F_K^{\mathrm{op}}$, and the cited extension theorem makes it preserve finite colimits. Equivalently, $F_K$ preserves finite limits.

source.place: Theorem 7.6.17, first paragraph; Propositions 7.5.5-7.5.6 and 7.5.28; parameter-cone construction as in section 6.4

proof.text: We prove the equivalence of $F_K$ by induction on the largest length of a nonidentity chain; the empty category has length $-1$ and its comparison is the identity of the terminal quasicategory. For $k\in K$, let $\ell(k)$ be the largest length of a nonidentity chain starting at $k$. For nonempty $K$, remove the objects $S$ on which $\ell(k)$ is maximal, obtaining $J$. Any nonidentity arrow into $s\in S$ would extend a longest chain starting at $s$, a contradiction; hence these objects satisfy the source hypothesis of the gluing lemma. For $s\in S$ put $B_s=(s/K)\setminus\{1_s\}$; both $J$ and every $B_s$ have strictly smaller length and are finite, including when there are parallel arrows. Write $M_sX=\lim_{B_s}X$. The source-gluing lemma describes a coherent $K$-diagram as its diagram on $J$ together with the cones at $S$, and gives the homotopy-pullback formula for its mapping spaces. We will use that formula, including the path in the pullback, rather than a pullback of Hom sets. Also $qM_sX\simeq\lim_{N(B_s)}qX$ for a Reedy fibrant $X$: induct on the same length, its ordinary cone equations give $\lim_KX=(\lim_JX)\times_{\prod_{s\in S}M_sX}\prod_{s\in S}X_s$. Apply the Brown localization lemma to this pullback, whose right-hand leg is a finite product of matching fibrations. The source-gluing mapping formula applied to constant testing diagrams gives exactly this homotopy-pullback description of the limit after localization. Thus the inductively identified lower cone and matching cones identify the entire limiting cone, not just its apex. Finite products are iterated pullbacks over $1$, so this proves their preservation too. Boundary restrictions are Reedy fibrant by the Reedy lemma. This argument supplies these specified matching-cone comparisons and their naturality in $X$.

First prove conservativity. For a strict map $f:X\to Y$ in $R_K$ whose components become invertible, construct a Reedy fibration $p:Z\to X$ with $fp$ componentwise in $W$. On $J$, the inductive equivalence makes $f|_J$ invertible in $L(R_J)$; the refinement clause of Brown fractions, applied to $R_J$, gives a Reedy fibration $p':Z'\to X|_J$ with $(f|_J)p'$ componentwise in $W$. For each $s$, form $P_s=M_sZ'\times_{M_sX}X_s$, which exists since $X_s\to M_sX$ is a fibration. On $J$, $qp'$ is a componentwise equivalence, since both $q(fp')$ and $qf$ are. Step 5 therefore makes $q(M_sp')$ an equivalence. The Brown pullback comparison makes $q(P_s\to X_s)$ an equivalence, and hence so is $q(P_s\to X_s\xrightarrow{f_s}Y_s)$. Brown refinement now gives a fibration $v_s:Z_s\to P_s$ with $Z_s\to Y_s$ in $W$. Use $Z_s\to P_s\to M_sZ'$ to attach the strict diagram at $s$. Its matching map is a composite of fibrations, and its relative matching map for $p$ is $v_s$, so $Z\in R_K$ and $p$ is a Reedy fibration. We have constructed $fp\in W_K$. Repeat this construction on $p$, whose localized components are equivalences, to obtain $r$ with $pr\in W_K$. In the homotopy category of $L(R_K)$, $p$ has a left inverse from $fp$ and a right inverse from $pr$; these inverses agree, so $p$, and then $f$, are invertible. Finally every morphism in $L(R_K)$ has a Brown fraction with trivial-fibration denominator. Applying what we just proved to its numerator shows that $F_K$ is conservative on all morphisms. No saturation of $W$ was presumed.

source.place: Theorem 7.6.17, conservativity paragraph; Corollary 7.5.19 and pullback preservation

proof.text: Every coherent $H:N(K)\to L\mathcal C$ is equivalent to $qX$ for a Reedy fibrant strict $X$. By the induction on $J$, choose $X'$ representing $H|_J$. For each $s$, source gluing and step 5 identify its remaining datum with an arrow $H_s\to qM_sX'$. Brown fractions give an ordinary representative $Z_s\to M_sX'$ after replacing $H_s$ by an equivalent $qZ_s$; this uses essential surjectivity of $q$ and a trivial-fibration denominator. Factor $Z_s\to M_sX'$ as $Z_s\xrightarrow{\sim}X_s\twoheadrightarrow M_sX'$. The strict matching maps define $X\in R_K$. The same source-gluing statement extends the chosen equivalence on $J$ and the equivalences $H_s\simeq qX_s$, with their cone homotopies, to an equivalence $H\simeq qX$. This proves essential surjectivity without any coproducts in $\mathcal C$.

Prove surjectivity on components of mapping spaces with the compatibility homotopy retained. Let $X,Y\in R_K$ and let $a:qX\to qY$ be a coherent transformation. Induction on $J$ and the Brown fractions of step 1 in $R_J$ give a Reedy trivial fibration $s':Z'\to X|_J$ and $p':Z'\to Y|_J$ representing $a|_J$, together with a homotopy to that restriction. For $s\in S$ define
$$P_s=M_sZ'\times_{M_sX}X_s,\qquad T_s=P_s\times_{M_sY}Y_s.$$
Here $P_s\to M_sY$ uses $M_sp'$. The map $P_s\to X_s$ is a trivial fibration: limits send the Reedy trivial fibration $s'$ on $B_s$ to a trivial fibration, and we pull it back along $X_s\to M_sX$. The map $T_s\to P_s$ is a fibration, being a pullback of the matching fibration for $Y$. In the localization, the component $a_s$ composed with $qP_s\to qX_s$ and the chosen lower homotopy give a section of $qT_s\to qP_s$: this is exactly the path between the two composites to $qM_sY$ in the source-gluing mapping formula. Both displayed ordinary pullbacks are sent to coherent pullbacks by the Brown localization lemma. Apply the coherent-section clause of [lem-coef-brown-slice-fraction-calculus] over $P_s$ ($W$ is retract closed). It gives a trivial fibration $t_s:Z_s\to P_s$ and a strict map $Z_s\to T_s$ over $P_s$, representing this specified section in the slice. Its projections supply compatible maps $Z_s\to X_s,Y_s,M_sZ'$. Thus they attach to $Z'$ and define strict maps $s:Z\to X$, $p:Z\to Y$; the relative matching map for $s$ at $s$ is precisely $t_s$. Hence $s$ is a Reedy trivial fibration. The homotopy in the slice and the already fixed homotopy on $J$ match the path data of the source-gluing formula, so the coherent fraction $qp(qs)^{-1}$ is homotopic to $a$ in the entire functor category. This proves surjectivity on mapping-space components; it does not try to glue only equality classes of component maps.

source.place: Theorem 7.6.17, final paragraph; Proposition 7.4.11 and Corollary 7.6.13; explicit relative-matching pullbacks

proof.text: Combine steps 6-8 with step 4 and apply [lem-coef-finite-colimit-approximation] to $F_K^{\mathrm{op}}$. Its source and target have finite colimits by step 4, and it preserves them. Conservativity is unchanged by taking opposites, so step 6 supplies that hypothesis. To check the approximation triangle, an arrow $F_K^{\mathrm{op}}(X)\to H$ in the opposite target is an arrow $H\to F_K(X)$ before reversal. Choose $e:H\simeq F_K(Y)$ by step 7. Step 8 supplies an arrow $u:Y\to X$ in $L(R_K)$ with $F_K(u)e$ homotopic to the given arrow. Reverse this triangle and use $e^{-1}$: it is exactly an arrow $X\to Y$ in the opposite source and an equivalence $H\to F_K^{\mathrm{op}}(Y)$ making the two target arrows equal in the homotopy category, as the cited statement requires. The approximation theorem therefore makes $F_K^{\mathrm{op}}$, and hence $F_K$, a coherent functor equivalence. The Reedy localized inclusion in step 1 gives the inverse-diagram comparison for $\mathcal C$, completing the induction.

Apply the result to $\mathcal C=\mathcal A^{\mathrm{op}}$ and $K=I^{\mathrm{op}}$. Opposite arrows turn the given initial object into a terminal object, pushouts into pullbacks, the factorization $C$ then $W$ into $W^{\mathrm{op}}$ then $C^{\mathrm{op}}$, and the two pushout-stability hypotheses into exactly the Brown hypotheses used above. The original degree strictly decreases on $K$. Taking opposites of the resulting equivalence gives the displayed comparison in the question: $\operatorname{Fun}(I^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal A^{\mathrm{op}})^{\mathrm{op}}=\operatorname{Fun}(I,\mathcal A)$ and reversal of simplices gives $\operatorname{Fun}(N(I)^{\mathrm{op}},L^{\mathrm{op}})^{\mathrm{op}}=\operatorname{Fun}(N(I),L)$. Opposite localization follows from its universal property by testing against opposite targets; the two canonical comparisons agree before localization with evaluation followed by $q$, so the same universal property identifies their factorizations. Step 7, or the essential surjectivity of this equivalence followed by the object-surjectivity clause of Brown fractions (step 1) for $R_K$, says that every coherent diagram is equivalent to the localization of an actual strict diagram. At a singleton this says every object of $L$ is equivalent to $qX$. For $I=\varnothing$ both sides are terminal. The singleton has degree $0$; for the stated span give $1$ degree $0$ and $0,2$ degree $1$. These checks introduce none of the excluded model-category or coproduct hypotheses.
